title: Too Much AI May Harm Student Confidence — Study
paragraphs: Generative AI tools such as chatbots have quickly become part of everyday life for many university students. However, a growing body of research suggests that relying too heavily on them may be linked to lower confidence and higher levels of stress.

In a study published in 2026 in the journal BMC Psychology, researchers led by Wenlong Wang surveyed 1,623 undergraduate students in China. The students answered questions about academic stress, anxiety, burnout and self-efficacy, which is a person's belief in their ability to deal with challenges and succeed. They were also asked how strongly they depended on AI for thinking, solving problems and doing their schoolwork.

The researchers found that students under greater academic pressure tended to depend more on AI. In turn, heavier reliance on AI was linked to higher levels of burnout and anxiety. According to the researchers, students who relied more on AI felt less capable of dealing with academic challenges on their own, and this lower sense of ability was connected to greater burnout and anxiety.

Another study, published in the journal Frontiers in Psychology in July 2026, surveyed 428 students at five universities in eastern China. It found that students with lower confidence in their academic abilities were more dependent on AI, whereas more confident students tended to solve problems themselves. Some students quoted in media coverage described feeling unable to start assignments without AI.

Importantly, neither study proves that AI causes students to lose confidence. It is also possible that students who already lacked confidence were more likely to turn to AI in the first place. In addition, the BMC Psychology study did not measure how often students actually used AI.

Nevertheless, the researchers do not recommend banning AI. Instead, they suggest that schools should help students build confidence through support and step-by-step feedback, and teach them to use AI critically as a tool that supports their own thinking. As one article on the research put it, AI is most useful as "a scaffold for learning rather than a substitute for it."
